analysis.investment_thesis: BBTC is the standout magic formula candidate of this set: EBIT/EV earnings yield of ~26% (EBIT INR 3,136 Cr ÷ EV ~INR 11,883 Cr) and ROCE of 35.5% — both in the top decile globally — driven primarily by its ~50% consolidated stake in Britannia Industries, which trades at the Wadia holding-company level at a massive structural discount (EV/EBITDA of 3.66× vs Britannia's own ~45× P/E). The conglomerate discount is the opportunity.
key_strengths: Top-decile on BOTH magic formula metrics simultaneously: earnings yield ~26% and ROCE 35.5% — an extremely rare combination
Underlying Britannia Industries asset is a durable FMCG compounder with strong brand moat, being valued at the holding-company level at a fraction of subsidiary market value
Consistent and growing FCF: INR 2,017 Cr in FY25; OCF positive 5/5 years; operating income CAGR of 11.2% over 9 years
key_risks: Holding company discount may never fully close — Wadia Group complexity and 74% promoter concentration structurally limit re-rating
Conglomerate structure (tea plantations, auto components, healthcare, real estate) obscures true earning power and makes segment analysis difficult
Tea/coffee plantation business is exposed to weather cycles, labour costs, and commodity pricing — low-ROIC drag on the consolidated entity
red_flags: FY23 net loss of −INR 534 Cr driven by −INR 781 Cr 'other income' (investment write-downs) — recurring risk given large investment portfolio
Borrowings spiked from INR 1,211 Cr (FY22) to INR 6,542 Cr (FY23) then normalised to INR 1,574 Cr (FY25) — evidence of leveraged investing activity that could repeat
Low liquidity: promoter at 74.04%, DII at only 1.42% — thin free float means price discovery is impaired and exit could be difficult at scale
analysis.detailed_analysis:
BBTC scores strongly on both magic formula dimensions. With EV/EBITDA of 3.66× on a consolidated entity generating INR 3,468 Cr EBITDA and INR 3,136 Cr EBIT, the earnings yield of ~26% is extraordinary — you are paying roughly 4 years of operating earnings for the entire enterprise. ROCE of 35.5% reflects Britannia's exceptional capital efficiency flowing through the consolidation. Revenue (INR 18,298 Cr) and operating income (INR 3,136 Cr) CAGRs of 8.5% and 11.2% over 9 years demonstrate that these are not distorted one-off numbers.

The structural reason for the discount is transparent: BBTC's ~50% stake in Britannia (market cap ~INR 1,10,000+ Cr) implies the Britannia stake alone is worth ~INR 55,000 Cr, yet BBTC trades at a market cap of INR 10,650 Cr. Holding company discounts of this magnitude (80%+) are unusual even in India. The FY23 loss and the FY22–23 debt spike from leveraged investing are genuine risks, but the operating cash flow engine (5/5 positive OCF years; FCF growing to INR 2,017 Cr) demonstrates the underlying business health. This is precisely the kind of mispriced, misunderstood business the magic formula is designed to surface.
